_readme: Physical model parameters for the MuJoCo arm simulation. Single source of truth:
controller parameters are NOT stored here, they come from App/application/s5_site.c
and the firmware CMake options through the bridge DLL (M2b).
status: measured = real measurement, estimated = rough estimate from a document,
assumed = modelling assumption, derived = computed from other entries in this file.
Every entry carries source and status; nothing here is validated on hardware.

meta.coordinate_convention: Sagittal plane x-z. Hanging arm = q 0 rad. Positive joint angle = forward flexion (+x), matching the firmware zero and sign (s5_site.c gravity_zero_rad = 0).

timestep_s.source: physics step only; controller periods are added in M3

height_m.source: D4 user decision 2026-10-26: everyday desk height

top_length_m.source: typical desk depth, only used to place the collision surface

edge_x_m.source: front edge of the table top, measured from the world origin where the arm hangs

collision_enabled.source: M1 keeps the desk as the mount only. With the shoulder 0.30 m above the top and a 0.77 m arm, a straight forward sweep passes through the desk above ~25 deg, so the S5 free-air sweep and a desk in front cannot both exist. Enable for the T5 desk task after the sitting posture is decided.

column_height_m.source: D4 user decision 2026-10-26: seat shoulder height minus desk height; also the table-edge-to-shoulder-axis height, so one number keeps both aligned

column_radius_m.source: support post size, not modelled from the drawing

shoulder_offset_x_m.source: horizontal bracket from the post top back to the shoulder axis: the user sits about 0.2 m behind the desk edge, so the hanging upper arm clears the desk front face

upper_link_m.source: 2026-10-08 user measurement, shoulder axis to elbow axis (L1)

upper_mass_kg.source: 3MF volume 2026-10-08 x ABS 1.1 g/cm3, 100% infill; screws/bearings/straps not included

upper_com_fraction.source: uniform link, centre of mass at mid length

forearm_link_m.source: 2026-10-08 user measurement, elbow axis to the outermost forearm cuff (L2)

forearm_com_fraction.source: uniform link, centre of mass at mid length

elbow_motor_mass_kg.source: bare M3508 mass, hardware reference 6.2; sits on the elbow axis

upper_radius_m.source: visual only, exoskeleton does not collide in M1

lateral_offset_y_m.source: User SolidWorks view 2026-10-26: the links run along the outside of the arm and the cuffs wrap it, so the exoskeleton plane is offset from the arm axis. Must stay above arm radius + link half width (0.045 + 0.035) to avoid interpenetration; 0.10 m is a placeholder until measured on the bench.

body_mass_kg.source: default until the user provides height and mass

height_m.source: default until the user provides height and mass

length_fraction_of_height.source: Winter, Biomechanics and Motor Control of Human Movement, Table 4.1 / Drillis-Contini segment length ratios

radius_m.source: collision radius for the table contact, visual only otherwise

length_fraction_of_height.source: Winter Table 4.1 / Drillis-Contini segment length ratios

radius_m.source: collision radius for the table contact

length_fraction_of_height.source: Winter Table 4.1 / Drillis-Contini segment length ratios

radius_m.source: collision radius for the table contact

straps.model_note: Each cuff is a soft ball joint (equality connect) at the centre of the band. The human-side attachment point is placed in the band plane (y = lateral offset), so the two points coincide at q = 0 and the constraint starts without a pull. A ball joint is deliberate: a rigid weld cannot work because the exoskeleton elbow axis sits 5.5 cm above the human elbow, which locks elbow bending.

distance_from_shoulder_m.source: band around the middle of the upper arm

human_distance_from_elbow_m.source: band on the proximal half of the human forearm

exo_distance_from_elbow_m.source: human 0.3255 + 0.10 - exo upper link 0.27; keeps the exoskeleton marker level with the human one at q = 0

solref_timeconst_s.source: soft band; lower = stiffer, 0.02 s is roughly a stiff velcro band

solref_dampratio.source: critically damped constraint; the stiffness is a placeholder, so the interaction-force level must be scanned in M5 before quoting any force
